name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+22 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats even without Wilson on the ballot
Oliver Gilbert's large fundraising edge over Te Mayonna Brown ($1.28M vs $313K raised)
Heavy outside spending against Gilbert ($2.1M) is the main sign of Republican interest
No public polling; prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 96%
model.rationale: The seat's D+22 lean and Gilbert's clear financial advantage over Brown point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat, and markets price the race similarly. The absence of polling and the outside money aimed at Gilbert justify trimming the expected margin slightly below pure fundamentals, not changing the outcome.
model.watch: Any polling showing single digits, or a late wave of outside spending signaling a genuine Republican opening, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Florida's 24th District, anchored in Miami-Dade County, is a heavily Democratic seat opening up with Frederica Wilson's retirement. Democrat Oliver Gilbert faces Republican Te Mayonna Brown in a district that has leaned roughly 22 points toward Democrats. No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate finances, and market pricing.

Gilbert has raised more than four times what Brown has collected, though outside groups have spent heavily against him. Prediction markets still price a Democratic hold at about 96 percent. The seat's strong lean makes a Republican upset possible only under an unusually large shift; the forecast expects Gilbert to win comfortably, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
